description: A file extension is a set of characters that helps the operating system identify the file type and determine which application software should open it. This is a crucial topic for the computer awareness section of competitive exams.

sections.title: Document and Text Files
sections.description: Files primarily used for saving, reading, and editing text-based content.

key_associations.extra_info: The most common word processing file format. In versions after MS Office 2007, the 'x' stands for XML.
Saves text without any rich formatting. It is typically opened in simple text editors like Notepad.
Developed by Adobe, it is used to view, share, and print documents exactly as intended across all platforms.
Supports basic text formatting (like bold, italics) and is primarily used by WordPad.

sections.title: Spreadsheet, Presentation, and Database Files
sections.description: Office suite files used for analyzing, presenting, and storing structured data.

key_associations.extra_info: Used to organize data in rows and columns and perform complex mathematical calculations.
Used for creating professional slide shows and visual presentations.
A plain text file widely used to transfer tabular data between different spreadsheets or databases.
Used to create, store, and manage relational databases.

sections.title: Image and Graphics Files
sections.description: Formats utilized for saving pictures and photographs with various quality and compression techniques.

key_associations.extra_info: The most widely used lossy compression format for digital photographs and web images.
Supports transparent backgrounds and uses lossless compression; highly popular for web graphics.
Primarily used for short, looping animations and low-resolution graphics.
An uncompressed raster graphics file format that retains high quality but is generally very large in file size.

sections.title: Audio and Video Files
sections.description: Extensions used to store multimedia content such as sound tracks and moving pictures.

key_associations.extra_info: The most popular digital audio format globally, used for compressing sound without significant loss of quality.
The most widely used video format for storing, streaming, and sharing video content over the internet.
Developed by Microsoft, this format plays synchronized audio and video data.
A standard format used mainly on Windows for saving high-quality, uncompressed audio.

sections.title: Compressed, Executable, and Web Files
sections.description: Extensions required for installing software, running programs, or reducing the size of large files.

key_associations.extra_info: Used to bundle one or more files into a single archive to easily share and reduce overall storage size.
Used to install or run software programs natively within the Windows operating system.
The standard file format used to distribute and install mobile applications on the Android operating system.
Files containing code used to structure and create web pages, which are then read and rendered by web browsers.

sections.title: Important Facts
sections.description: Basic and highly exam-relevant facts regarding computer file extensions.

important_facts.fact: A dot ('.') is strictly used by the operating system to separate the primary file name from its extension (e.g., 'resume.pdf').

In MS Office 2007 and all subsequent versions, the 'x' added at the end of the legacy file extensions (making them .docx, .xlsx, .pptx) stands for XML (Extensible Markup Language), a format that makes files lighter and less prone to corruption.
